source.title: Batch Normalization Amplifies Memorization and Privacy Risks
source.authors: Ngoc Phu Doan; Chong-Yan Gu; Ihsen Alouani

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices. Some results are presented only in figures, without recoverable numerical values.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares models with and without batch normalization on corrupted-label and out-of-distribution fitting, and reports training-loss trends. These are related measures of training behavior, but the study does not directly test the claim’s full zero-training-error or optimization conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports leave-one-out influence, membership-inference, and BNReg results; these concern memorization influence, privacy, or the paper’s mitigation method rather than the claim versions’ named outcomes. They are not catalog rows. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares training with and without BN, extending the training-speed question to corrupted-label examples and additional architectures. Its near-zero noisy-set loss also bears on V1's corrupted-label fitting component, although whole-training-set classification error is not established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that BN accelerates and increases outlier memorization and membership-inference leakage, provide a conditional mechanism based on the exact BN backward pass, and propose BNReg to mitigate memorization. The theoretical amplification depends on batch geometry and the scale-to-spread ratio; it is not an unconditional guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: Compares BN and no-BN training while measuring corrupted-label/OOD fitting and training-loss trends; it does not replicate the original training-error studies’ full recipes or evaluate their stated model-size and stopping conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies dataset, architecture, label-flipping/outlier ratio, learning rate, batch size and optimizer; the reported result says the BN/no-BN memorization difference persists across several of these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: BN models perfectly fit injected OOD examples, whereas no-BN models have approximately three percentage points lower accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization improves fitting of an injected OOD training subset assigned a shared target label.

record.problems: For the directly relevant fitting comparisons, many results are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. The paper does not report per-model training classification error or test the width, stopping-time, initialization, shortcut, or stability conditions in the versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version rows were extracted from the paper’s privacy attack, leave-one-out influence, BNReg, or theoretical margin analysis because those results do not measure the outcomes named by the versions. Figure-only clean-set loss in Figure 4 is retained as R4, with state cannot_determine.

untested.parts: Whole-training-set zero or near-zero classification error; a model-size threshold; fully randomized labels; initialization details; systematic effects of width, early stopping, and regularization. Near-zero loss is stated only for the noisy subset.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons of plain networks with identity shortcuts.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Initial stability thresholds, catapult recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Tolerance to higher learning rates, the original sigmoid/VGG/Inception settings, and Fixup comparisons. Appendix E.1's final accuracies at 10^-3 do not establish learning-rate tolerance.

missing.what: Training-loss comparisons for Lenet, ResNet34, and ResNet50 on clean and noisy CIFAR-10 subsets across corruption ratios 5%–30%. The text explicitly states faster convergence with BN. R3 covers only Lenet at 5%; R4 overlooks the textual clean-subset result.
missing.locator: Appendix C.3, Figure 25; use the section's subset definitions because the figure caption reverses them.

missing.what: Corrupted-label training accuracy across matched optimization checkpoints: BN models have higher accuracy at the same epoch budget. Record this separately from comparisons matched on testing loss or utility, which do not directly measure training speed.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. Deliberate label corruption is relevant here because V1 explicitly includes corrupted labels. Relative endpoint accuracy alone supplies neither a near-zero-error verdict nor a training-speed verdict. The record's V6 limits_scope label for R5 is unsupported: missing learning-rate-tolerance measurements are untested parts, not demonstrated limitations.

versions.untested_parts: Tests relative fitting of corrupted-label and OOD examples with versus without BN. Does not report exact training classification error for each model, establish near-zero error across sufficiently large models, or sweep width, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
The paper does not study two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems or student width relative to teacher width.
The paper does not compare plain networks with identity-shortcut networks or test shortcut effects on depth-related training error.
The paper does not compare initialization schemes or test how initialization affects trainable depth.
The paper does not study learning rates relative to a stability threshold, loss curvature, or edge-of-stability dynamics.

Reports faster loss reduction in selected BN versus no-BN settings, including noisy samples, but does not test tolerance to higher learning rates or the specific sigmoid, VGG, and Inception settings in the version.

conditions.value: different ratios k; exact values not stated in the main-text result

rows.measure: Classification accuracy on flipped-label samples as an indicator of fitting/memorization.
rows.baseline: Models without BN (red curves); exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Models incorporating BN consistently achieve higher accuracy than models without BN across all datasets and all ratios; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: Aggregate result stated across five named architectures, four datasets and varying ratios. The paper does not give the plotted accuracies in the supplied text, so the extent of training-error reduction cannot be quantified.
rows.check: Higher corrupted-label accuracy with BN does not establish near-zero training error or demonstrate that fitting is incomplete. Restrict the V1 link to CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; split off MNIST and FashionMNIST. Absolute accuracies and clean-training-set errors are unavailable.
